purpose: Build and seal a held-out conceptual-code question set over ~/code/agent-lab with gold file spans (gap 13), then score Recall@5 and MRR for the incumbent embedder (live vLLM Nemotron-3-Embed-1B, 127.0.0.1:8231) against a genuinely different, free, locally-served alternative embedder (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, served from the isolated vLLM 0.30.0 prefix) over identical chunking and identical top-k, to settle whether the compatibility-only evidence in native-rag.json / hf-memory-model-qualification.md (gap 0, gap 8) generalizes to a measured retrieval-quality comparison, and whether at least one alternative embedder now has a local quality/latency qualification against the incumbent (gap 5).
preregistered: Write >=30 questions from actually reading agent-lab source files (not filenames), with 1-based file:line gold spans, disjoint from fixtures/rag-note.md. Seal the question set (sha256) before any retrieval run. Chunk the repo identically for both arms (fixed line window/overlap, same include dirs). Index each arm's chunks into its own disposable-Qdrant collection using that arm's own embedding endpoint and a fixed passage/query prefix convention documented for that model. Score Recall@5 (line-range overlap >=1 line with any gold span, top-5) and MRR for both arms with one script applying the same overlap rule. A result where the alternative embedder is close to or exceeds the incumbent's Recall@5/MRR would refute the incumbent-only quality claim (supports_incumbent=false); a result where the incumbent is clearly ahead supports keeping the incumbent as the qualified choice pending a further latency/cost tradeoff study. No re-run planned regardless of outcome; a run-time architectural mismatch (context-length limit on one arm) is recorded as a limitation, not smoothed over by re-chunking after seeing scores.

result: Measured, on this sealed 35-question set over agent-lab's tools/.claude/workflows/tests/docs code: incumbent Nemotron-3-Embed-1B (2048-dim, 4096-token context) Recall@5=0.971, MRR=0.853; alternative bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-dim, 512-token context) Recall@5=0.771, MRR=0.592. The incumbent embedder outperforms this free alternative on both metrics on this corpus and question set. A material contributor to the alternative's lower score is its much smaller native context window, which forced per-item chunk loss (725/2485 chunks, including partial loss on 3 of 35 gold-span files) that the incumbent did not suffer (6/2485 lost, none gold-span files) -- this is a genuine capability difference between the two models, not solely a retrieval-quality difference, and is reported as such rather than folded into the headline numbers.

verdict_impact.explanation: This is the first held-out, cross-model, line-span-scored retrieval benchmark run for this layer (settling the executable_now next_check for gaps 0, 8, 13, and giving gap 5 a local quality/latency qualification for one alternative embedder). It supports keeping Nemotron-3-Embed-1B as the qualified choice on this evidence, but only partially settles gap 5 ('Nemotron 8B and other embedders') since the alternative served here is bge-small-en-v1.5, not Nemotron 8B, and only one alternative (not a sweep) was measured; gap 0/8's broader 'quality, not just compatibility' question is now measured for one alternative and could change again with a stronger or larger-context alternative embedder.

limitations: One alternative embedder only (bge-small-en-v1.5), not Nemotron 8B named in gap 5's text; Nemotron 8B was not available/served in this unit due to time budget.
bge-small-en-v1.5's 512-token context caused real, differential chunk loss vs the incumbent's 4096-token context; the reported Recall@5/MRR gap is not attributable to embedding quality alone.
35 questions is a modest sample; individual question hit/miss can shift Recall@5 by ~2.9 percentage points each.
Corpus is a fixed slice of agent-lab (tools/, .claude/workflows/, tests/, docs/, 4 extensions); not the whole repository or other repositories.
Mean query latency figures are single-run wall-clock on a shared host under this unit's own load; not a controlled throughput benchmark.

Questions were authored by the same agent running the benchmark, from real code reading; no independent human or second-model review of question/gold-span correctness was obtained given this unit's time budget.
